newsitem.title: UK: British house prices leap 1.6 percent in October - Halifax.
newsitem.headline: British house prices leap 1.6 percent in October - Halifax.

text.p: British house prices rose a hefty 1.6 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis in October, Britain's leading mortgage lender the Halifax Building Society, said on Tuesday.
On an annual basis, house price inflation is now 7.1 percent compared with the 5.2 percent reported last month, the Halifax house price index showed.

"Although such a strong monthly rise is unlikely to be repeated over the next two to three months, house price inflation now is likely to end the year in excess of our forecast of five percent, probably around seven percent," a Halifax statement said.
It said it expected a similar rise to follow in 1997.
The sharp rise in October prices followed a small 0.1 percent increase in September, revised up from an initial 0.1 percent fall, and a 0.4 percent gain in August.
The latest figures suggested confidence in the housing market is continuing to improve in line with recent increases in transactions, the Halifax said.
Prices paid by first-time buyers rose by 1.1 percent in October, taking the annual rate of inflation up to 7.1 percent, from 4.8 in September.
The average price paid by first-time buyers was 47,963 pounds ($78,530).
Prices of new houses fell by 0.8 percent in October, the index showed, following a 0.3 percent rise in September. But they remain 2.1 percent higher than a year ago.
The average price of a new house was 69,051 pounds in October. ($1=.6107 Pound)
